newsitem.title: UK: Lead hangs on to rally momentum in AM kerb.
newsitem.headline: Lead hangs on to rally momentum in AM kerb.

text.p: Buoyant lead held the market's focus on Friday as prices toyed with the $700 level, the highest in a month, amid a widening backwardation.
The other base metals on the London Metal Exchange (LME), however, showed decidedly less enthusiasm for the upside and copper and aluminium languished off recent highs.
The lead market was caught short when fresh options-related buying emerged late on Thursday, and the trend continued on Friday morning, traders said.
Three months delivery lead ended the morning kerb at $697 per tonne, up strongly from Thursday's kerb close of $675, and just off the day's high of $700.

Alongside the price rise, lead's cash to threes snapped into a backwardation due to tightness in April dates. Cash/threes were last at $21/$23 compared to level at Thursday's kerb close and $6/$7 contango at the start of the week.
April/May backwardation was bid at $18, while a lender for April was found at $22.
Analysts said there was nothing fundamental behind lead's sharp move higher, but the technical tightness was typical of the market.
Copper prices, meanwhile, drifted lower on end-of-month profit taking after this week's surge to $2,415 left the market overheated.
An LME stocks decline of 3,475 tonnes was largely in line with expectations and did little to support the market.
Copper ended the kerb at $2,371, down $22 from Thursday's finish and below the $2,380/$85 resistance area.
"Copper is going to come down a bit. I can see back at $2,330 area before it tries higher again," a trader said.
Solid support at the $2,313 chart point was also expected to hold up the market. On the upside the $2,400 and then $2,450 levels remained eventual targets, analysts said.
Aluminium was underpinned by a bigger than expected 11,075-tonne stocks decline on Friday morning, but the news was not enough to light a fire under the market.
It ended the kerb just $2 easier at $1,650, the nearby support level, and off Thursday's highs around $1,670.
Nickel was steady at $8,060, just $10 lower. The market was watching developments at Russia's Norilsk Nickel plant, where workers said they may strike next month because of wage arrears.

Management at Norilsk said on Friday that any strike could jeaopordise a repayment schedule for salary and holiday arrears. Management and labour are due to meet on Saturday. Zinc prices were barely firmer, up $1, at $1,228 after a stocks drawdown of 4,550 tonnes.
But tin edged lower to end the kerb $65 down at $5,815 after a stock increase of 170 tonnes.
